subject: Proposed $12 Million Property Tax Override
overview: The council debated a proposed $12 million Proposition 2 1/2 override referendum to address a structural budget deficit and fund schools, DPW, and the library. The meeting also included public hearings on rezoning petitions, business licenses, and infrastructure transfers.

items.title: Petition for Zoning Amendment: 196 and 200 Boston Ave
items.summary: Approved a petition from Cummings Properties LLC to change the zoning of two parcels on Boston Avenue from Industrial I to Office 202.

items.title: Public Hearing: Finance Auto Body License
items.summary: Approved a Class 4 automotive repair license for 26 R. Mystic Avenue pending a six-day comment period, with a requirement for police and code enforcement feedback on parking congestion.

items.title: National Night Out Presentation
items.summary: The Medford Police Community Engagement Unit presented plans for the National Night Out event on August 2nd at Hormel Stadium.

items.title: Overnight Tractor Trailer Parking
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that Medford Police address overnight commercial truck parking on Commercial Street and Route 16.

items.title: Appointment: Board of Election Commission
items.summary: Confirmed the appointment of Erin DiBenedetto to the Board of Election Commission for a term expiring in 2026.

items.title: Call for State Primary Election and Early Voting
items.summary: Approved the call for the state primary election on September 6, 2022, and established early in-person voting dates at City Hall from August 27th to September 2nd.

items.title: Proposition 2 1/2 Override Referendum
items.summary: The council debated a proposed $12 million property tax override for school and city operations, which was ultimately tabled for one week following an objection under Rule 21.

items.title: Consent Agenda and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the records of the June 22nd meeting and committee reports regarding the budget and the Eversource project.

items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions
items.summary: Approved resolutions of condolence for World War II veteran Oscar Green and congratulations for Gwendolyn B. Lee on her 100th birthday.

items.title: Public Hearing: Starbucks Extended Hours
items.summary: The council kept the public hearing open for 90 days regarding a request for 5 a.m. opening hours at the College Avenue Starbucks.

items.title: Public Hearing: Order of Taking for Freedom Way and Stephen R. Drive
items.summary: Approved the transfer of roadway parcels from the school department to the city to facilitate future repairs using Chapter 90 funds.

items.title: Sign Appeal: Volta Charging
items.summary: Approved a sign appeal for electric vehicle charging stations with digital displays at 760 Fellsway, including an agreement to provide city public service announcements on the screens.

items.title: Senior Property Tax Exemptions
items.summary: Referred a proposal to increase property tax exemptions and income limits for seniors over 65 to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Infrastructure and Public Welfare Resolutions
items.summary: Approved resolutions regarding Wellington Circle signage, Wellington Station beautification, SNAP restaurant program outreach, and river cleaning between Craddock and the pedestrian bridge.

items.title: Support for Childcare Access Legislation
items.summary: Approved a resolution in support of state bill H.4795 to expand access to high-quality, affordable early education and care.
